domain-information: A show producer develops a new show proposal and submits it to the channel manager.
A show producer hires a regisseur to lead the production of the approved show.
A show producer reviews the budget plan of a show with the channel manager before production starts.
A regisseur plans the shooting schedule for the show.
A regisseur directs the filming of a show which produces raw footage.
A regisseur collaborates with the film editor to finalize the show cut.
A film editor takes raw footage and turns it to a complete show cut based on the regisseur’s vision.
A film editor presents the show cut to the producer in a post production meeting.
A channel manager reviews new show proposals to decide which ones to approve.
A channel manager puts a show into a broadcast slot.
A channel manager analyses audience feedback of a show.

domain objects.name: Show Producer
domain objects.description: A person responsible for developing and overseeing a television show's production.

domain objects.name: Show Proposal
domain objects.description: A document outlining a new show's concept and details for approval.

domain objects.name: Show
domain objects.description: A television program produced for broadcast.

domain objects.name: Budget Plan
domain objects.description: An estimated cost outline for producing a show.

domain objects.name: Shooting Schedule
domain objects.description: A planned timeline for filming sessions.

domain objects.name: Show Cut
domain objects.description: The completed version of a show after editing.

domain objects.name: Regisseur
domain objects.description: A director responsible for creative direction during filming.

domain objects.name: Filming
domain objects.description: The process of recording footage for a show.

domain objects.name: Raw Footage
domain objects.description: Unedited video material recorded during filming.

domain objects.name: Film Editor
domain objects.description: A specialist who assembles and refines footage into the final show cut.

domain objects.name: Post Production Meeting
domain objects.description: A session where the final show cut is reviewed and discussed.

domain objects.name: Channel Manager
domain objects.description: An executive responsible for approving, scheduling, and evaluating shows on the channel.

domain objects.name: Broadcast Slot
domain objects.description: A scheduled time segment for airing a specific show.

domain objects.name: Audience Feedback
domain objects.description: Responses and opinions collected from viewers after broadcast.

associations.description: The Show Producer creates and submits the Show Proposal.
The Show Producer reviews and manages the Budget Plan with the Channel Manager.
The Show Producer hires and works with the Regisseur for show production.
The Regisseur directs and oversees Filming.
Filming contributes recorded material to the Show.
The Regisseur creates and follows the Shooting Schedule.
Filming produces Raw Footage for post-production.
The Film Editor uses Raw Footage to assemble the Show Cut.
The Film Editor creates the final Show Cut from edited footage.
The Regisseur reviews and refines the Show Cut to match creative goals.
The Film Editor presents the Show Cut during the Post Production Meeting.
The Show Producer reviews the final Show Cut in the Post Production Meeting.
The Channel Manager reviews and approves Show Proposals.
The Channel Manager approves or adjusts the Budget Plan for production.
The Channel Manager schedules the Show in a Broadcast Slot.
The Channel Manager evaluates Audience Feedback for channel performance.
Audience Feedback reflects the reception of the Show.
